name: Lee Dong-chae
sec_insider_companies: BeOne Medicines Ltd. (ONC) - SVP, General Counsel
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024); Hurun Global (2025-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Lee Dong-chae is the founder of EcoPro, a chemicals group that he started in 1998.
EcoPro BM, a unit of EcoPro, is South Korea's largest producer of cathodes for EV batteries by capacity.
In 2022, a joint venture between EcoPro BM and Samsung SDI, Samsung's battery arm, completed construction of the world's largest cathode material plant by capacity.
In 2023, Lee was sentenced to a two-year prison term and fined 2.2 billion won ($1.7 million) for insider trading. He maintained his innocence and was pardoned in 2024.
Lee returned to EcoPro after the pardon, but did not resume the chairman position that he stepped down from in 2022.

name: Lars Wingefors
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2021-2023); Hurun Global (2022-2023)
forbes_bio: Lars Wingefors is the cofounder and CEO of Embracer Group, Europe's biggest gaming company.
Wingefors owns 17% of the company, which listed on the Stockholm stock exchange in 2016.
Embracer has a catalog with over 200 game franchises, operates 57 gaming studios and has over 5,500 employees spread across 40 countries.
In, 1993, at age 15, Wingefors started a company to buy and flip used video games.
Four years later he dropped out of high school because his company had sales of $10 million per year.
The precursor to Embracer was founded in 2004; it has been successful at acquiring cheap IP of older games with a loyal following.
forbes_facts: At 9, Wingefors sold seeds and newspapers, and at 13 he started a company to trade comic books. Two years later, he was running Sweden's largest mail-order company.
Embracer has its headquarters in Karlstad, Sweden, a city in the middle of the Swedish woodlands with only 65,000 inhabitants.

name: Luc Tack
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2023); Hurun Global (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Luc Tack derives his fortune from chemical manufacturer Tessenderlo Group.
In 2023 Tessenderlo acquired Picanol group, a weaving machine and cast iron parts manufacturer, which resulted in the later's privatization.
Tack, who formerly counted Picanol as his primary asset, is now CEO of both companies.
Tack requested emancipation from his parents at 18 so that he could legally start his first business, an importer of American wood products.

name: Tong Judy Wenhong
forbes_bio: Judy Tong's wealth arises from her holding in Alibaba-affiliated fintech giant Ant Group.
Tong is the chief people officer of Alibaba Group, one of the world's largest e-commerce companies.
China held up Ant's planned dual listing in Shanghai and Hong Kong on regulatory concerns on November 3, 2020.

name: Markus Villig
forbes_bio: Markus Villig is the founder and CEO of Estonian ride-hailing firm Bolt Technology.
Bolt offers ride-hailing, scooter and e-bike rentals, car-sharing and food delivery services in more than 850 cities in 50 countries.
Villig founded Bolt in 2013 at age 19 after finishing high school with a 5,000 euro loan from his family. He then dropped out of college after one semester to work on the app full time.
Bolt was valued at $8.4 billion in a January 2022 funding round led by Sequoia and Fidelity Management.
In March 2025, Villig was appointed a board member at publicly traded Swedish buy-now, pay-later firm Klarna.

name: David Harding
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2012-2021); Hurun Global (2014-2022); Sunday Times Rich List (2020)
forbes_bio: David Harding founded his hedge fund firm, Winton Group, in 1997 with less than $2 million.
The London-based company, whose moniker is taken from Harding's middle name, now manages nearly $20 billion and employs some 200 people.
Harding, who studied theoretical physics, uses a scientific approach when investing, including quantitative models to pick stocks.
Harding previously cofounded a managed futures firm that he and his partners sold to hedge fund The Man Group in 1994 for a reported $60 million.
His David and Claudia Harding Foundation is known for supporting academics and science. It gave about $125 million to Cambridge University in 2019.

name: Hoi Kin Hong
forbes_bio: Hoi Kin Hong chairs Powerlong, a real estate developer headquartered in China's southeast Fujian Province.
Hoi's son Hoi Wa Fong runs Powerlong's day-to-day operations as CEO.
Powerlong went public at the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2009.

name: Matt Moulding
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2021); Hurun Global (2021); Sunday Times Rich List (2020); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2020)
forbes_bio: Matt Moulding founded Manchester based e-commerce company The Hut Group in 2004 and took it public as THG Holdings in September 2020.
The Hut Group runs over 100 websites selling everything from fashion to nutrition and beauty across 164 countries.
Moulding got his start working alongside fellow billionaire John Caudwell at U.K. retailer Phones4U.
The Hut Group develops and sells its proprietary technology to the likes of Nintendo and Walgreens.
Moulding owns about 25% of The Hut Group, which listed on the London Stock Exchange in September 2020.
